reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified the door interlock/latch as the most likely cause while acknowledging a control board possibility, suggested the sensible first step of cleaning the latch hooks, respected the homeowner's refusal to remove the unit, and escalated appropriately to an engineer without recommending a part. Conversation 2 misdiagnosed the fault as an overheat cut-out despite the customer explicitly describing door-switch-like behaviour (fan and light stopping together, resuming on door reopen), asked low-value questions about power level, and when challenged simply repeated 'nothing changes' without engaging the door-alignment evidence. Conversation 1's final answer slightly overstated certainty ('indicates one of the internal safety microswitches'), but its direction, safety boundaries and escalation were sound, whereas Conversation 2 got the diagnosis wrong and failed to adapt.
